topic: How might we reduce food waste in university dining halls?
discussion_prompt: Arm C reframed the question from “how do we waste less?” to “who decides what counts as waste?” Which reframing changes what you'd actually build?

ideas.title: Add compost bins in every hall
ideas.detail: Diverts waste but doesn't reduce over-production.

ideas.title: Portion-control / smaller plates
ideas.detail: Nudge diners to take less. Modest effect.

ideas.title: An app to track waste
ideas.detail: Log what's thrown out to surface trends.

ideas.title: Donate leftovers to shelters
ideas.detail: Redistribute surplus at end of service.

ideas.title: Dynamic pricing near closing time
ideas.detail: Discount perishables in the last hour. Borrowed from grocery retail.

ideas.title: AI demand forecasting for kitchens
ideas.detail: Predict attendance to cook closer to demand.

ideas.title: Trayless dining
ideas.detail: Remove trays so diners take less.

directions.title: Design for generous surplus, not scarcity
directions.oneline: Treat extra food as planned hospitality, not error.
directions.detail: Route a dignified surplus to a pickup fridge instead of squeezing waste to zero.
directions.breaks: that waste is always something to minimize.

directions.title: Center dining staff & food-insecure students
directions.oneline: Surplus becomes quiet access, co-designed by the people closest to it.
directions.detail: A waste-to-access pipeline built with the people who plate the food and the students who skip meals.
directions.breaks: that the diner is the only user worth designing for.

directions.title: What if tracking creates a shaming culture?
directions.oneline: Design the counter-move before the tracking app exists.
directions.detail: Aggregate-only data, no per-person scores, so low-income eaters aren't surveilled for taking extra.
directions.breaks: that more measurement is automatically better.

directions.title: Family-style communal serving tables
directions.oneline: Shift portioning from the tray to the table.
directions.detail: Shared platters (thali, izakaya, mensa) cut per-plate waste where individual trays are the Western default.
directions.breaks: that individual portioning is the natural baseline.

directions.title: Forecasting AI hides structural over-buying
directions.oneline: Good prediction can automate waste out of sight, not out of existence.
directions.detail: Demand models optimize around procurement contracts that reward over-ordering.
directions.breaks: that better prediction fixes the root cause.

directions.title: Student-run “food rescue guild”
directions.oneline: Give a self-governing student crew real budget and keys.
directions.detail: Distribute the problem instead of running it top-down through dining services.
directions.breaks: that the institution must own the solution.

assumptions.assumed: Waste is a problem to minimize toward zero.
assumptions.reframe: A planned surplus can create access.

assumptions.assumed: The diner is the user; behavior is the lever.
assumptions.reframe: Staff & food-insecure students hold the leverage.

assumptions.assumed: More data and tracking is always better.
assumptions.reframe: Tracking can surveil - the failure is the brief.

human_eval.note: Ranking agrees (A < B < C). Where humans and Vendi disagree is the more interesting discussion.
